q: The Banach-Alaoglu theorem states that the closed unit ball of the dual space X* is compact in the weak-* topology. This is used in analysis to:
opts: Prove every bounded sequence has a norm-convergent subsequence
Extract weak-* convergent subsequences from bounded sequences in X*, enabling compactness arguments in function spaces
exp: Banach-Alaoglu: B_{X*} is weak-* compact. This is the main compactness tool in functional analysis: bounded sequences in L^∞, measures, etc. have weak-* convergent subsequences. It is the foundation of many existence proofs (e.g., invariant measures via Markov-Kakutani fixed point theorem).
